currentContext.expansion: Capital deployment in FY 2025-26 was directed towards manufacturing expansion, R&D infrastructure and Pharma CRDMO facilities, with the Company stating that '₹11,508 million of capex deployed towards manufacturing expansion, R&D infrastructure and Pharma CRDMO facilities, including capacity additions at Jambusar, Panoli, Jaipur and Lodi (Italy)'. In pharma, the CRO facility in Hyderabad strengthens discovery and development capability while the commissioning of the kilo-lab facility in Lodi, Italy is expected to enhance the ability to serve global pharmaceutical customers; the pharma vertical is described as progressively transitioning from a development-stage CRDMO to a commercial-stage, revenue-generating business, with capabilities extending to ADCs and large molecules under evaluation. The Biologicals platform expanded its global presence across the US, Brazil, Mexico, UK and Europe on the peptide technology platform, with a bio-nematicide registration approved in the U.S. and a differentiated biological nematode solution commercially launched in Mexico; the Seattle R&D Centre serves as the global hub for innovation, field validation, product development and commercial support. On the manufacturing footprint the Company is advancing towards a smart-factory model and digital lighthouse designation aligned with Industry 4.0, executing no/low-touch manufacturing, digitalisation and automation initiatives, smart steam-trap retrofits and a smart fuel monitoring system, alongside heat pumps, energy-efficient screw chillers and automated flow controllers; waste-stream recycling scale-up eliminated downstream utility loads for distillation and Multi-Effect Evaporator operations while capturing 10-30% specific energy savings. Renewable energy rose to over 10.0% of total electricity consumption, water interventions (dry vacuum pumps replacing steam jet ejectors, RO efficiency, Sewage Treatment Plants) delivered a 68% increase in water recycling and recovery volume and lowered total wastewater generation by 16% towards zero-liquid-discharge objectives, and following biodiversity risk assessments across all operational sites and R&D centres, plans are finalised to develop a dedicated biodiversity park featuring over 100,000 native saplings in FY27.

risks.risk: Prolonged cyclical downturn and inventory correction in the global crop protection market
risks.note: The global crop protection market has witnessed a prolonged cyclical downturn shaped by industry-wide inventory corrections; consolidated AgChem exports declined 19% in FY2026 and consolidated revenue fell 16% YoY, showing how directly the cycle transmits to the top line.

risks.risk: Dependence on global innovator partners' offtake schedules
risks.note: Revenue moderation was attributed primarily to deferred offtake schedules by global innovator partners and inventory rationalisation across key markets - delivery phasing sits with the customer, not the Company, so revenue timing is only partly controllable.

risks.risk: Weather and monsoon dependence in the domestic business
risks.note: The monsoon season, influenced by La Nina conditions, produced unseasonal and erratic rainfall that adversely impacted crop cycles and farm productivity; abiotic stress (weather) acted as a major headwind that lowered sales volume in the Domestic segment.

risks.risk: Regulatory action on the product portfolio, particularly biologicals
risks.note: The business environment was challenged by a regulatory ban on biologicals and by regulatory transitions in biologicals, which disrupted domestic demand during the year.
Continued volatility in input costs and volatile raw-material prices are cited as ongoing pressures on the cost base alongside the demand downturn.
Pricing pressures in the generic agrochemicals segment were named as a driver of revenue moderation, indicating limited pricing power outside differentiated and patented molecules.

risks.risk: Farmer economic stress and working-capital constraints in the trade channel
risks.note: Economic stress on farmers led to demand disruption and significant value erosion across the crop protection industry, with working-capital constraints in trade further challenging the domestic environment.

risks.risk: Process safety and occupational health hazards in chemical manufacturing
risks.note: The BRSR discloses an employee LTIFR of 0.29 per million person-hours and one high-consequence work-related injury in FY 2025-26 (nil in FY 2025), with the risk managed through HAZOP/What-If studies, HIRA/JSA, Pre-Startup Safety Reviews, LOTO, permit-to-work, third-party Quantitative Risk Assessments and Critical Risk Identification exercises.

one-line thesis: Despite H1 revenue decline due to weather and regulatory headwinds, PI is on track with 8-10 new product launches, strong pharma CDMO pipeline, and biologicals recovery in Q4; the shift from AgChem-only to diversified life sciences is accelerating, with non-AgChem segments now contributing meaningfully.
financial scorecard: Revenue: -16% YoY (Rs. 18,723 Cr); EBITDA/margin: Resilient at ~28-29% (above guidance of 26-27%) due to product mix; PAT (rptd): Down YoY due to higher R&D/overheads; PAT (normalized): Adjusted for one-off waste processing costs in pharma; Order book: $1.25B; Net debt: Low, cash-rich with no urgent deployment pressure
guidance: Revenue growth: Mid-single-digit for FY26; Margin: Maintains 26-27% annual EBITDA margin guidance; Order inflow: Recovery expected in Q4; Capex/commissioning: Two new plants nearing commissioning (AgChem + electronic chemicals), capex focused on CDMO and biologicals scale-up
order book & pipeline: $1.25 billion as of Q2FY26; visibility for FY27 guidance to be provided in Q4FY26
segment / subsidiary detail: AgChem Exports: -16% YoY, volume-led decline due to destocking; Domestic Agri: -5% H1 YoY, hit by rains and biologicals ban; Pharma CRDMO: +54% YoY H1, 2 new clients onboarded, 6 late-stage programs (Phase II/III); Biologicals: $10-12M annual revenue, regulatory ban lifted in India, sales restarting in Q4; Electronic Chemicals: 5-6 products commercialized, pipeline growing, new plant commissioning imminent
growth verticals / optionality: Biologicals to grow 3-4x over next 3-5 years; Pharma CDMO to reach profitability by FY27 with 4 large pharma clients targeted; Electronic chemicals to scale in 1-2 years; Potential inorganic M&A in domestic agro or tech areas
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin expanded to ~50-52% due to favorable product mix; EBITDA margin at 28-29% (above guidance) due to operational efficiencies; Pharma margins temporarily pressured by one-off waste costs and high R&D; Biologicals margins negative currently, investment phase until FY28
capex / expansion: Two new plants nearing commissioning: one for AgChem, one multi-product plant for electronic chemicals; Capex focused on CDMO infrastructure, biologicals R&D (Hyderabad center), and scale-up of specialty chemical production
capital allocation: Cash-rich with no urgent deployment; evaluating inorganic opportunities in domestic agro and global tech; prioritizing organic growth in pharma CDMO, biologicals, and electronic chemicals; no dividend or buyback mentioned
risks & watch-items: Weather volatility impacting domestic demand; prolonged regulatory delays in biologicals outside India; biotech funding slowdown affecting pharma CDMO conversions; Chinese overcapacity depressing global agchem prices; geopolitical uncertainty around U.S. tariffs
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but emphasizes strategic momentum in new products, pharma pipeline, and biologicals; confident in FY26 recovery from Q4 and long-term transformation into diversified life sciences player
non-obvious takeaways: Contract assets of Rs. 450 Cr represent revenue already recognized but deferred delivery — not inventory, signaling strong customer commitment despite market softness; biologicals revenue is small ($12M) but has 25%+ CAGR potential and unique peptide platform

themes.title: Agrochemicals & crop-input cycle recovery
themes.need: Crop-protection is recovering off a brutal trough, and Q1FY27 shows domestic branded volume decoupling from generic exports. RALLIS grew revenue only 7% yet lifted EBITDA 23% to a ~18.0% margin (+230bps) as domestic B2C rose 19% on +15% volume while exports COLLAPSED 28% (volume -35%) on Chinese pricing, and its seeds EBITDA margin went 26% to 30% on a rice/maize/millet mix versus price-controlled cotton - though PAT +31% is flattered by an INR 35cr employee-provision reversal of which INR 24cr is genuinely one-time, so normalise before extrapolating. The monsoon is the live variable: as of 8-Jul seasonal rainfall was ~15% below normal with kharif acreage ~21% below last year. SUMICHEM delivered record FY26 profitability; INSECTICID/DHANUKA/SHARDACROP ride premiumization + technicals; COROMANDEL/GNFC/CHAMBLFERT/GODREJAGRO add fertilizers + integrated agri.
themes.driver: Monsoon catch-up and kharif acreage recovery from ~21% below last year; domestic B2C volume against continued Chinese export price pressure; new molecule launches and biologicals scale-up.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: PI Industries manufactures and distributes agro chemicals and operates through a single reportable business segment, 'Agro Chemicals', serving both domestic and international markets with customers ranging from institutional buyers to end consumers. Its core model is custom synthesis and manufacturing for global agrochemical innovators built on complex process chemistry, alongside a domestic branded crop-protection business. During the year the Company continued its transition from a pure agri-chemical company to a diversified life sciences enterprise, extending into pharmaceutical, global biologicals and specialty / electronic chemicals.

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic Indian crop protection market (branded/differentiated products, farming community)
- Export markets - exports contributed 81.08% of total turnover (BRSR Section A)
- Markets served: 28 states in India and 24 international countries (BRSR Section A)
- Global agrochemical innovators under long-term custom synthesis partnerships
- Global pharma and biotech innovators via PI Health Sciences CRDMO (business development in the US, Japan and Europe)
- Biologicals markets with regulatory credentials in the US, Brazil, Mexico, Spain and the UK

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: $1.25 billion as of Q2FY26; visibility for FY27 guidance to be provided in Q4FY26

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: Mid-single-digit for FY26; Margin: Maintains 26-27% annual EBITDA margin guidance; Order inflow: Recovery expected in Q4; Capex/commissioning: Two new plants nearing commissioning (AgChem + electronic chemicals), capex focused on CDMO and biologicals scale-up

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Biologicals to grow 3-4x over next 3-5 years; Pharma CDMO to reach profitability by FY27 with 4 large pharma clients targeted; Electronic chemicals to scale in 1-2 years; Potential inorganic M&A in domestic agro or tech areas

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management remains optimistic about the medium- to long-term outlook; early signals from global innovator partners - indicative offtake plans and a stabilised order book - suggest industry inventory normalisation is underway
- Healthy reservoir levels entering Kharif FY2026-27 and a stabilised domestic biologicals portfolio following regulatory disruptions position the Company to benefit from improving market conditions
- The AgChem business is expected to maintain strong momentum, driven by a healthy order book, a robust pipeline of commercialised and late-stage molecules and deepening partnerships with global innovators
- FY 2025-26 was marked by cyclical revenue headwinds across the global AgChem sector, with revenue trajectory hit by moderated AgChem exports amid customer scheduling, plus erratic weather and regulatory transitions in biologicals domestically
- Gross-margin support from mix: new products contributed 18% of AgChem Exports revenue and five new molecules were commercialised during the year (15+ over three years)
- Global CRDMO market was valued at approximately USD 196 billion in 2023 and is projected to reach approximately USD 329 billion by 2029, growing at a CAGR of about 9.0%, as global biotech and pharma increase outsourcing driven by pipeline complexity, capital-efficiency requirements and the need for specialised capabilities
- PI Health Sciences revenue grew 40% YoY with positive momentum through new partnerships and an expanded active customer base
- Biologicals demand opening: US EPA registration and commercial launch of PI's foliar bionematicide, the world's first foliar-application nematode product, creates a new use-case model for nematode management in standing crops
- Domestic Agri Brands performance was mixed, impacted by adverse weather, lower crop prices, regulatory disruptions in biologicals and elevated channel inventory
- Government schemes extending affordable institutional credit to smallholder farmers can support a gradual improvement in effective demand for quality agrochemical products, including branded, differentiated and biological crop-protection solutions
- In FY 2025-26 the CSM order book held steady, indicating an intact pipeline
- A stabilised order book and indicative offtake plans from global innovator partners are cited as early signals of inventory normalisation
- R&D pipeline of 90+ molecules supported by 700+ scientists across 4 R&D centres
- Agri Brands: four new products launched with a strong pipeline of 20+ products at different stages of development
- PI Health Sciences conversion of development-stage engagements is anchored on a growing late-stage clinical pipeline

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin expanded to ~50-52% due to favorable product mix; EBITDA margin at 28-29% (above guidance) due to operational efficiencies; Pharma margins temporarily pressured by one-off waste costs and high R&D; Biologicals margins negative currently, investment phase until FY28

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Cash-rich with no urgent deployment; evaluating inorganic opportunities in domestic agro and global tech; prioritizing organic growth in pharma CDMO, biologicals, and electronic chemicals; no dividend or buyback mentioned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Capital deployment in FY 2025-26 was directed towards manufacturing expansion, R&D infrastructure and Pharma CRDMO facilities, with the Company stating that '₹11,508 million of capex deployed towards manufacturing expansion, R&D infrastructure and Pharma CRDMO facilities, including capacity additions at Jambusar, Panoli, Jaipur and Lodi (Italy)'. In pharma, the CRO facility in Hyderabad strengthens discovery and development capability while the commissioning of the kilo-lab facility in Lodi, Italy is expected to enhance the ability to serve global pharmaceutical customers; the pharma vertical is described as progressively transitioning from a development-stage CRDMO to a commercial-stage, revenue-generating business, with capabilities extending to ADCs and large molecules under evaluation. The Biologicals platform expanded its global presence across the US, Brazil, Mexico, UK and Europe on the peptide technology platform, with a bio-nematicide registration approved in the U.S. and a differentiated biological nematode solution commercially launched in Mexico; the Seattle R&D Centre serves as the global hub for innovation, field validation, product development and commercial support. On the manufacturing footprint the Company is advancing towards a smart-factory model and digital lighthouse designation aligned with Industry 4.0, executing no/low-touch manufacturing, digitalisation and automation initiatives, smart steam-trap retrofits and a smart fuel monitoring system, alongside heat pumps, energy-efficient screw chillers and automated flow controllers; waste-stream recycling scale-up eliminated downstream utility loads for distillation and Multi-Effect Evaporator operations while capturing 10-30% specific energy savings. Renewable energy rose to over 10.0% of total electricity consumption, water interventions (dry vacuum pumps replacing steam jet ejectors, RO efficiency, Sewage Treatment Plants) delivered a 68% increase in water recycling and recovery volume and lowered total wastewater generation by 16% towards zero-liquid-discharge objectives, and following biodiversity risk assessments across all operational sites and R&D centres, plans are finalised to develop a dedicated biodiversity park featuring over 100,000 native saplings in FY27.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but emphasizes strategic momentum in new products, pharma pipeline, and biologicals; confident in FY26 recovery from Q4 and long-term transformation into diversified life sciences player

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated in-house R&D platform: 700+ scientists, 200+ PhDs and a proprietary library of 80,000+ compounds, with end-to-end capabilities across discovery, process development, formulation and manufacturing
- Active pipeline of over 90 molecules, described as among the strongest in the Company's history, with more than 60% in advanced stages of development
- Ranked among the top five globally in Custom Synthesis and Manufacturing, built on three decades of trust, technical depth and complex chemistry
- Proprietary IP origination: Pioxaniliprole is the first insecticide molecule developed by an Indian company to receive ISO approval, and the first time an Indian company plans to take a novel active ingredient from original discovery through to global commercialisation
- Long-term partnerships with global innovators for complex, early-stage and patented molecules rather than transactional engagements, supporting margin resilience
- Proprietary biological IP through the Plant Health Care (now PI AgSciences) acquisition, including PREtec peptide technology and regulatory credentials in the US, Brazil, Mexico, Spain and the UK
- Advanced manufacturing capability - continuous flow, safer phosgenation, green catalyst and biotechnology platforms; proof-of-concepts for advanced drying (RDDC) and liquid-liquid extraction demonstrated up to 40% energy savings and a 15% reduction in batch cycle times
- Enterprise-wide digital backbone: went live on SAP S/4HANA across a multi-business, multi-geography footprint
- ESG standing: featured for the third consecutive year in the S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook, ranking among the top 2 percentile of ESG-rated companies worldwide, with CSA score rising from 68 to 77, and inclusion in the Dow Jones Best in Class Indices for Emerging Markets

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Weather volatility impacting domestic demand; prolonged regulatory delays in biologicals outside India; biotech funding slowdown affecting pharma CDMO conversions; Chinese overcapacity depressing global agchem prices; geopolitical uncertainty around U.S. tariffs

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Contract assets of Rs. 450 Cr represent revenue already recognized but deferred delivery — not inventory, signaling strong customer commitment despite market softness; biologicals revenue is small ($12M) but has 25%+ CAGR potential and unique peptide platform

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demand cycle] Deck acknowledges cyclical headwinds: soft demand in the global agrochemical industry, generics pressure continuing with global agrochemical companies, pricing under pressure, and delayed and uneven monsoon impacting Kharif sowing and partially postponing domestic sales.
- [Input costs] Increase in input material prices due to ongoing geopolitical tensions impacted gross margin, though the deck also states commodity prices are showing a positive trend.
- [CRDMO headwinds] PI Health Sciences faces a slowdown in biotech funding and geopolitical challenges, with the Q1FY27 revenue decline attributed mainly to customer order phasing; the deck reports PIHS revenue contracted 25% YoY and PIHS remains loss-making at the PBT level post intercompany eliminations.
- [Order book] Order book is said to continue supporting the growth outlook for new products in FY27, with build-up of pipeline projects through new strategic partnerships entered in the last 12 months and improved business development and R&D pipeline visibility over the next 1-2 years.
- [Awards] India's Top Value Creator 2025 - Agro Chemicals by Dun & Bradstreet; Most Preferred Workplace 2025-26 by Marksmen Daily; British Safety Council Sword of Honour for the Udaipur site (October 2025); Business Leader of the Year - ESG at Chemtech Leadership & Excellence Awards 2026.
